description: Core concepts, threats, and defenses in digital security

cia_triad.confidentiality: Information accessible only to authorized parties
cia_triad.integrity: Data is accurate and unmodified by unauthorized parties
cia_triad.availability: Systems and data accessible when needed by authorized users

malware.virus: Attaches to legitimate files; spreads when executed
malware.worm: Self-replicates across networks without user action
malware.trojan: Disguised as legitimate software; creates backdoors
malware.ransomware: Encrypts files and demands payment for decryption
malware.rootkit: Hides in system; gives attackers persistent access

social_engineering.spear_phishing: Targeted phishing aimed at specific individuals

network_attacks.dos_ddos: Denial of Service; overwhelms target with traffic
network_attacks.sql_injection: Inserts malicious SQL code into database queries
network_attacks.xss: Cross-Site Scripting; injects scripts into web pages
network_attacks.zero_day: Exploits unknown vulnerability before patch exists

cryptography.symmetric: Same key for encryption and decryption (AES, DES)
cryptography.asymmetric: Public key encrypts, private key decrypts (RSA, ECC)
cryptography.pki: Public Key Infrastructure; digital certificates verify identity

authentication_methods.mfa: Multi-Factor Authentication; combines multiple verification types
authentication_methods.oauth: Authorization framework allowing third-party access without sharing credentials
authentication_methods.zero_trust: Never trust, always verify; assumes breach at all times

network_security.firewall: Monitors and filters network traffic based on rules
network_security.ids_ips: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems; detect and block attacks
network_security.vpn: Virtual Private Network; encrypted tunnel for remote access
network_security.dmz: Demilitarized Zone; isolated network segment for public-facing servers
network_security.nat: Network Address Translation; hides internal IP addresses

security_frameworks.nist: US National Institute of Standards and Technology cybersecurity framework
security_frameworks.iso_27001: International standard for information security management
security_frameworks.owasp: Open Web Application Security Project; OWASP Top 10 lists critical web vulnerabilities
security_frameworks.mitre_attck: Knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques

vulnerability_management.cve: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures; standardized vulnerability IDs
vulnerability_management.cvss: Common Vulnerability Scoring System; 0–10 severity scale
vulnerability_management.penetration_testing: Authorized simulated attacks to find vulnerabilities
vulnerability_management.bug_bounty: Programs rewarding security researchers for responsibly disclosing vulnerabilities

best_practices.patching: Regularly update software to fix known vulnerabilities
best_practices.least_privilege: Give users minimum access necessary for their role
best_practices.backups: Regular backups stored offline or offsite
best_practices.incident_response: Planned procedure for detecting, containing, and recovering from breaches
